input.quote: Customer commits to purchase at least USD 2,000,000 of Services in each of the next three years on a take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights.
input.rationale: Section 9 provides only cause-based, insolvency, security/service-level, force-majeure and warranty termination rights; no party has a convenience right, and Section 2.1 expressly strips Customer of termination rights across a three-year take-or-pay commitment (Section 8.1). Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months fails the fallback. Vendor has no convenience right, so no Vendor-side deletion is needed. We inserted the preferred 30-day convenience right with a pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees as a new Section 9.4 (9.4 is unused in the outline) and conformed Section 2.1 so the take-or-pay language does not negate it; 60-90 days' notice remains available as a fallback.

proposal.summary: Add Customer termination for convenience on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund; align Section 2.1 take-or-pay language
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a Customer right to terminate for convenience on thirty (30) days' notice with a refund of prepaid Fees, since a three-year commitment with no exit right is outside our playbook, and conformed Section 2.1 so it does not negate that right. If you need a transition runway, we can move to 60-90 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.text: Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, without penalty or early-termination charge, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid Fees for the period after the effective date of termination. Vendor has no right to terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience during a committed term.

ops.newText: without reduction, subject to Customer's termination rights under this Agreement, including Section 9.4.
